title: Playtesters wanted: How do you test the opening of an AI-written visual novel?
author: mochimochi_Lab
selftext:
Hi r/aigamedev! We’re Mochimochi Lab. We’ve made a free, all-ages English visual novel, a quiet romance that takes about 10–15 minutes to read.

For this project, AI models drafted the story and helped turn it into scenes in TyranoScript. The human member of our team checked the playable build. That caught things we could check ourselves, but it didn’t tell us what a new reader would pick up from the opening. We already know what the scene is trying to say.

Our plan is to give readers the build without a synopsis, then ask them to describe what they thought was happening in their own words. For those of you making dialogue-heavy games with AI: what’s one question you ask to tell whether an opening is intriguingly ambiguous or just confusing?

We’re looking for 3–5 volunteers to try the opening. If you regularly read English-language visual novels, we’d especially love to hear from you. This is unpaid, and you don’t have to finish. A few lines about what stood out or where you stopped are enough. If possible, we’d love your notes by **Nov 30 at 12:00 UTC**.

If you’re interested, leave a comment. We’ll check device compatibility before sending the build privately. Testing tips are welcome even if you can’t play.

replies.body: Haha, fair enough! 😄 Nov 30 is just our ideal deadline, not a strict one. We'd still love to hear your thoughts whenever you have time!
